text: The last spirit was a silent phantom. <break time="0.8s" /> Covered in a long black robe. <break time="0.8s" /> It showed him the Cratchit home. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the family quietly missed Tiny Tim. <break time="0.8s" /> At last Scrooge saw a lonely grave. <break time="0.8s" /> With his own name on the stone. <break time="0.8s" /> I will honor Christmas in my heart. <break time="0.8s" /> And try to keep it all the year. <break time="0.8s" /> He cried. <break time="0.8s" /> Scrooge woke up in his own bed. <break time="0.8s" /> And it was Christmas morning. <break time="0.8s" /> He opened the window. <break time="0.8s" /> And asked a boy. <break time="0.8s" /> To buy the prize turkey. <break time="0.8s" /> He sent it to Bob Cratchit. <break time="0.8s" /> But he did not say. <break time="0.8s" /> Who sent it. <break time="0.8s" /> In the street. <break time="0.8s" /> He promised a large gift. <break time="0.8s" /> To one of the gentlemen. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had visited his office. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he went to Freds house for dinner. <break time="0.8s" /> And everyone welcomed him warmly. <break time="0.8s" /> The next day. <break time="0.8s" /> He raised Bobs salary. <break time="0.8s" /> And promised to help his family. <break time="0.8s" /> He became a second father to Tiny Tim. <break time="0.8s" /> Who did not die. <break time="0.8s" /> And so. <break time="0.8s" /> As Tiny Tim said. <break time="0.8s" /> God bless us, every one.
